data.name: Mythic Lunar Ascendant
data.detailed_description:
Ancient-Style Work: The Mortal World Is All About Cultivation​

Urban Life Experience​

Leave the cave mansion to work as a "Chang'an West Market worker"—by day, copy scriptures at "Moyun Studio" (earning spirit stones and gaining insights); in the evening, play the pipa at "Shuiyue Tower" for extra cash (unlocking hidden storylines); late at night, help an old farmer drive away "field mice gnawing on spiritual roots" (triggering side quests).

Integration of Solar Terms Culture​

Fly kites at "Qujiang Pool" during the Spring Equinox (with a chance to obtain the "Spring Breeze Talisman"); make dumplings at "Zhongnan Mountain" during the Winter Solstice (restoring the entire party's status). Each limited-time activity for a solar term hides Chinese folk custom easter eggs (e.g., embroidering pouches to gift to NPCs during the Qixi Festival to increase favorability).

Closed-Loop System for Work Rewards​

Earned spirit stones can be used to buy magic treasures, hire guards, or donated to the "Cihang Abbey" in exchange for "Merit Value." The higher the Merit Value, the more likely to trigger "Heavenly Dao's Gift" events (e.g., immortals guiding breakthroughs), but it may also attract the attention of "hypocrites"...

▌ Divinization/Darkening: A Single Thought, Eternal Consequences​

Moral Balance System​

Every choice is labeled with "Heavenly Dao Tendency" (e.g., "Spare a little demon stealing spiritual grass" +1 Good) and "Human Desire Tendency" (e.g., "Take a demon pill to save villagers" +1 Evil). If the values cross the threshold, it will permanently alter Luo Hongxue's appearance (a moon mark appears between the brows when divinized, eyes turn crimson with flames when darkened) and her ability tree.

Materialization of Heart Demons​

When the "Heart Demon Value" fills up, the "Mirror Illusion" is triggered—confront the most feared obsessions in your heart (e.g., "people you failed to protect," "memories of betrayal"). Defeating it grants exclusive divine abilities; losing traps you in a permanent "Demonized DEBUFF."

Multi-Ending Truth​

5 main endings (Divinization/Demonization/Hermitage/Fallen Mortal/Chaos) + 12 side quest conclusions, with no "standard answer"—you can be the cold "New Lord of the Moon Palace" or a "Lost One" wandering the mortal world with regret, but every ending is met with an NPC's sigh: "You ultimately chose the hardest path."

content_descriptors.notes:
This game is a Chinese mythology-themed cultivation RPG, containing the following elements that require attention:

Nudity Content: Certain characters (such as the protagonist Luo Hongxue) wear outfits that reveal shoulders and legs in specific story scenes (e.g., Cave Mansion, Moon Palace Celebration). Body contours are suggested through draped clothing (visible shoulder and leg lines, no exposure of genitals). This is a "Sword-tier" tastefully sensual design, with no explicit sexual content.

Violence Content: Combat features fantasy/cartoonish styles (such as "Lunar Spell" or "Jade Rabbit Pestle" attacks). It includes non-realistic blood effects (e.g., skill light effects, energy explosions). There is no realistic bleeding, dismemberment, or high-impact violence.

Moral Themes: Contains a "Deification/Demonic Path" system (choices to become a god or fall into darkness), involving human nature dilemmas. However, it does not glorify violence, crime, or extreme behavior.

Other: No content related to suicide, horror, drug abuse, etc. The language is elegant and classical, with no vulgar expressions.
